items.method: Cross-read the single-name options tape (call-versus-put premium, call fraction and the heaviest same-session prints) against the options-structure corridor (negative dealer gamma, flip, put and call walls, expected move) and the intraday auction, then test that call-leaning signal against equity internals — broad market-heatmap breadth and the defensive-but-constructive sector rotation — to judge whether the call demand is the leading edge of an upside break or noise pinned inside a wall corridor, and anchor a direction-correct invalidation to the put-wall level the constructive index read mechanically depends on.
items.note: The genuinely new signature this window is that the derivative tape has rotated from the put-heavy hedging of the prior window to call-leaning single-name demand, and it is doing so while the cash market stays broad. Option premium is balanced-to-slightly-call at a 0.5656 call fraction — $1.250B of call premium against $0.960B of put premium across 12 tickers, 1228 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days — and the two most unusual prints are same-session calls: TSLA 355 calls at $35.2M on 43.4x open interest and MSFT 490 calls at $4.9M, with only a smaller GOOGL 345 put behind them. Underneath, market-heatmap breadth is broad at 68.13% of 134 constituents, an 8.13-point margin over the 60% line, and sector leadership is constructive with XLP and XLV both Leading. The structure model puts SPY in negative dealer gamma with spot near 764.83 wedged between the 764 put wall and the 765 call wall, about 3 points under the 768.11 flip and inside a plus-or-minus 2.48 expected move, with the intraday auction a Range day pinned to a 765.02 VWAP. So call demand is building against a still-broad tape at a mechanical inflection that has not yet triggered either way. Watch a reclaim of the 768.11 flip as the confirming trigger that flips dealers positive and releases the corridor upward; because breadth and leadership keep this a constructive index-level read, it is invalidated on a daily close below ~764.00 on SPY, which loses the 764 put wall in negative gamma and hands control to the downside.
items.title: The single-name options tape has flipped call-leaning (TSLA 355C $35.2M 43.4x OI, MSFT 490C) into a broad, constructive cash market (68.13% breadth) while SPY is pinned between the 764 put wall and the 765 call wall in negative dealer gamma just under the 768.11 flip — call demand pressing an untriggered corridor

items.method: Cross-read the sector-rotation RRG state for energy (XLE relative-momentum quadrant and acceleration) against the real-assets model's oil and broad-commodity scores and its energy-equity confirmation channel to locate where the two models agree and disagree on the energy node, then, finding no direction-correct price level on a committed-universe energy vehicle, withhold a tactical call rather than publish one that cannot be scored.
items.note: The new contested node this window sits in energy: the equity-rotation model and the real-asset model disagree on the same complex. The sector model is rotating specifically out of energy — XLE reads Peaking with acceleration turned negative at -0.32 even though its one-, three- and six-month relative momentum are still positive (3.69, 6.74, 3.22) — which is a leadership that is fading rather than breaking. At the same time the real-assets model reads the underlying commodity complex as firm: broad baskets DBC and PDBC both score 63.3 in uptrends, oil (USO) scores 49.8 with a strong 58.47% twelve-month push despite a soft -6.58% three-month pulse, and the model's own energy-equity confirmation for oil scores 74.9 off XLE direction. So relative-rotation work is leaving energy equities just as the commodity read underneath them stays supported — a divergence between where the price complex is and where the rotation is going. This is a structural observation, not a scoreable trade: no direction-correct price level on a committed-universe energy instrument is available this window, so a tactical energy call is withheld rather than published with only a working side. Watch whether XLE reclaims a Leading acceleration or the commodity complex rolls over to resolve which side is right; until an energy price level is in view, the node is carried as evidence for the equity brief, not as a call.
items.title: Energy is a contested cross-model node this window — the sector model is rotating out of XLE at a Peaking RRG state while the oil and broad-commodity complex holds firm (USO 49.8, DBC and PDBC both 63.3, XLE energy-equity confirmation 74.9)
